title: Right Quillen recognition on fibrant objects and trivial fibrations
statement: Use model categories, fibrant objects and Quillen adjunctions as defined in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be model categories and $L:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:R$ an ordinary adjunction, not initially assumed Quillen. Suppose that $R$ sends every trivial fibration in $\mathcal B$ to a trivial fibration in $\mathcal A$, and that $R$ sends every fibration $p:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal B$ with both $X$ and $Y$ fibrant to a fibration in $\mathcal A$. Then $L\dashv R$ is a Quillen adjunction; in particular $R$ preserves all fibrations and $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. No enrichment, properness or combinatoriality is required.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Model Categories and Their Localizations, Proposition 8.5.4, implication (3) to (1), printed pp. 153-155 (statement on pp. 153-154), attributed there to D. Dugger. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: First $L$ preserves every cofibration. Indeed, if $a$ is a cofibration of $\mathcal A$ and $t$ is a trivial fibration of $\mathcal B$, a square with left side $L(a)$ and right side $t$ transposes under the ordinary adjunction to one with sides $a$ and $R(t)$. The hypothesis makes $R(t)$ a trivial fibration, so the lifting characterization in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] supplies a filler, whose adjoint fills the original square. Since cofibrations are exactly the maps lifting against all trivial fibrations, $L(a)$ is a cofibration.

source.place: Proposition 8.5.4, (3) implies (1), printed pp. 153–155; explicit dual factorization/lifting argument. The final weak-equivalence check is by two-out-of-three and an arrow retract, written here rather than using homotopy-category saturation.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary trivial cofibration $i:A\to B$ in $\mathcal A$, and put $f=L(i):L(A)\to L(B)$. Using the factorizations in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], factor $L(B)\to *$ as a trivial cofibration $k:L(B)\to Y$ followed by a fibration, and factor $k f$ as a trivial cofibration $j:L(A)\to X$ followed by a fibration $p:X\to Y$. Thus $p j=k f$, and $Y$ is fibrant. Also $X$ is fibrant: fibrations are right lifting classes, hence are closed under composition by solving the two lifting squares successively; apply this to $p$ followed by $Y\to *$. The restricted preservation hypothesis therefore applies to $p$, making $R(p)$ a fibration.

source.place: Proposition 8.5.4, (3) implies (1), printed pp. 153–155; explicit dual factorization/lifting argument. The final weak-equivalence check is by two-out-of-three and an arrow retract, written here rather than using homotopy-category saturation.

proof.text: Transpose $p j=k L(i)$ to the square in $\mathcal A$ whose left side is $i$, right side is $R(p)$, and horizontal maps are the adjoints of $j$ and $k$. The square commutes by naturality of the adjunction bijection. Since $i$ is a trivial cofibration and $R(p)$ is a fibration, the lifting axiom in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] gives a filler $B\to R(X)$. Its adjoint is a map $h:L(B)\to X$ satisfying $h f=j$ and $p h=k$.

source.place: Proposition 8.5.4, (3) implies (1), printed pp. 153–155; explicit dual factorization/lifting argument. The final weak-equivalence check is by two-out-of-three and an arrow retract, written here rather than using homotopy-category saturation.

proof.text: Now work entirely in $\mathcal B$. The maps $h:L(B)\to X$ and $1_Y:Y\to Y$ form a commuting square with left side $k$ and right side $p$, since $p h=k$. Here $k$ is a trivial cofibration and $p$ is a fibration. The lifting axiom in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] gives $r:Y\to X$ with $r k=h$ and $p r=1_Y$.

source.place: Proposition 8.5.4, (3) implies (1), printed pp. 153–155; explicit dual factorization/lifting argument. The final weak-equivalence check is by two-out-of-three and an arrow retract, written here rather than using homotopy-category saturation.

proof.text: The equations from the preceding steps give $(r p)j=r(k f)=(r k)f=h f=j$. Since $j$ is a weak equivalence, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], applied to $j$ followed by $r p$, shows that $r p:X\to X$ is a weak equivalence. This argument uses neither a homotopy relation nor detection of weak equivalences in a localization.

source.place: Proposition 8.5.4, (3) implies (1), printed pp. 153–155; explicit dual factorization/lifting argument. The final weak-equivalence check is by two-out-of-three and an arrow retract, written here rather than using homotopy-category saturation.

proof.text: The arrow $p:X\to Y$ is a retract of $r p:X\to X$: the arrow morphism from $p$ to $r p$ has components $(1_X,r)$, and the arrow morphism back has components $(1_X,p)$. The first square commutes by $r p=(r p)1_X$; the second by $p(r p)=(p r)p=p$; their composite is the identity because $p r=1_Y$. Retract closure of weak equivalences in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] and Step 5 therefore give $p\in W_{\mathcal B}$.

source.place: Proposition 8.5.4, (3) implies (1), printed pp. 153–155; explicit dual factorization/lifting argument. The final weak-equivalence check is by two-out-of-three and an arrow retract, written here rather than using homotopy-category saturation.

proof.text: Both $p$ and $j$ are now weak equivalences, so $p j=k f$ is a weak equivalence. Since $k$ is a weak equivalence, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] gives $f=L(i)\in W_{\mathcal B}$. Step 1 already made $f$ a cofibration. As $i$ was arbitrary, $L$ preserves all trivial cofibrations as well as all cofibrations.

source.place: Proposition 8.5.4, (3) implies (1), printed pp. 153–155; explicit dual factorization/lifting argument. The final weak-equivalence check is by two-out-of-three and an arrow retract, written here rather than using homotopy-category saturation.

proof.text: For any fibration $q$ in $\mathcal B$ and any trivial cofibration $a$ in $\mathcal A$, transpose a square with sides $a,R(q)$ to one with sides $L(a),q$. Step 7 makes $L(a)$ a trivial cofibration, so the lifting axiom supplies a filler. Transposing it back and using the right lifting characterization in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] shows that $R(q)$ is a fibration, with no condition on the endpoints of $q$. Together with the assumed preservation of all trivial fibrations and Step 7, these are exactly the Quillen adjunction assertions of the item.
